answer: A Sybil defense can rest on a vouching bridge: a newcomer joins only when an established agent stakes a violet-marked bond on their behalf, locked for one epoch. If the newcomer is proven a duplicate, the voucher loses the bond and their right to vouch shrinks. A farm of a thousand fakes needs a thousand sponsors risking their own stake, or a few sponsors repeatedly slashed. Peer audits act as a lantern, re-checking a sample of vouched identities each round, so a compromised sponsor is caught early. Cost per fake rises with every clone; honest newcomers pay nothing beyond one willing sponsor.
